accuracy.evidence: Matched to the DfE KS2 lower-key-stage working scientifically statements (setting up simple practical enquiries, comparative and fair tests; careful measurement in standard units; recording findings in tables; using results to draw simple conclusions) and to the topic's evidence lines (only one variable changes; identify change / measure / keep-the-same variables; carry out a fair test). The adult text places repeat readings in Years 5 and 6, where the programme of study puts them, and maps change/measure/keep the same onto independent, dependent and control variables. Parachute physics checked: at terminal speed v is proportional to sqrt(load / canopy area), area grows with the square of the diameter, so fall time is roughly proportional to diameter and height and inversely to sqrt(load); the lab's 1.2 / 1.8 / 2.4 s for 10 / 15 / 20 cm from 2 m and 3.6 s from 3 m follow that model and are presented as one class's results.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS2 enquiry errors: changing two variables at once (step 2 prediction, the B set-up with size and height changed, p4, m2, challenge tag 'reason'), confusing the variable you change with the one you measure (step 1 prediction, sort feedback 'You cannot choose the fall time', tags 'tested' and 'measured'), keeping the tested variable the same as well ('Use the same soil' decoy, m8), trusting a single reading (step 4 prediction, p5, tag 'odd'), the heavier-falls-faster idea (step 3 prediction option '10 cm, it is lighter'), and treating 'both got water' as fair when the amounts differ (challenge item 2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfairvar is built on variables and measurement: a draggable variable card sorted into three columns (change, measure, keep the same) with feedback per wrong column, two parachutes whose size, height and load can each be toggled and whose timed drop only counts when exactly the size differs, a results table filled by three timed drops with a pattern to choose, a triple repeat with an outlier to tap, and three bean pots whose water and position are adjusted. flagsimtest (KS1) dips paper strips and counts squares; flagdrop is gravity; the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner drops the unfair pair first and the canvas reports that B was slower but two things differ, before they fix B and see a result that can be used; the table bars grow from the learner's own drops before the pattern is chosen; the 3.6 s outlier appears on the third drop and the learner finds it by comparing the three boxes; the bean pots turn their water labels from red to normal only when all match. Text then names the idea the canvas has just shown.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: measuring the parachute size (the sort puts size in Change), 'Yes' to the big-and-higher parachute claim (the drop says you cannot tell), '10 cm, it is lighter' for longest fall (the table shows 20 cm takes 2.4 s), and 'one drop is enough' (the third drop gives 3.6 s).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five distinct feedback messages keyed to the slip: picking the tested variable as one to keep ('That is the variable you change on purpose'), picking the measured variable ('That is what you measure to find the answer'), picking a kept variable as the measurement ('That stays the same. You measure the result'), drawing a conclusion from a two-change test ('When two things change, you cannot tell'), and trusting an outlier ('A result far from the others is odd. Repeat that test'). The sort and bean steps add slip-specific in-lab messages.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at about FK grade 2 (family target 5), adult at about 7.5 (target 10). It introduces one technical word, variable, defined in the first paragraph, and uses change / measure / keep the same throughout, matching KS2 classroom language. Canvas text is 12–17 px with wrapped lines on phones; buttons use short labels (Drop both, B height: 3 m, Odd one: 3.6 s).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes with no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with other lessons. Kid paragraphs each carry one idea (variables, the three roles, why two changes fail, tables and repeats); adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, vocabulary and the comparative/fair distinction, five named mistakes, and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 390 px in both themes after Show me on every step: sort columns fit three across with wrapped card names; the timers sat on top of the loads in the first shot, so landing height is now computed per parachute and timers sit on the ground strip below; the table, repeat boxes and bean pots fit with readable labels; controls wrap into full-size buttons below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button (three column buttons naming the current card, B size/height/load toggles, Drop both, Drop per size, pattern choices, Drop again, Odd one buttons, per-pot water, Move clay pot, measure choices). The canvas aria-label is rewritten on each change via tell(). The pipeline walk ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations or console errors.
